atAGlance: Giò heo hầm is braised or simmered pork leg, usually with gelatinous skin, tender meat, broth, and vegetables.
whatItIs: Giò heo hầm is simmered pork knuckle, usually cooked until the skin and tendon turn soft in broth with vegetables, herbs, or medicinal aromatics depending on the shop.
howToEnjoy: Eat slowly and expect gelatinous skin, tender meat, and broth rather than a dry pork plate. Rice or noodles can make it a full meal.
howLocalsOrder: Order giò heo hầm when you want soft pork knuckle and broth. Ask if it comes with noodles, rice, or vegetables before choosing sides.
worthKnowing: In Vietnamese soups and stews, the prized texture is collagen-rich and tender; travelers who prefer lean meat may want another pork order.
goodToKnow: Hầm means simmered. Expect gelatin-rich pork knuckle in broth, so the pleasure is tender skin, soft meat, and a warming bowl rather than a caramelized kho plate.
